jei.aromara.brazier.aromara.alchemical_m: Feeds hungry players, draining vis from the aura for each one fed.
jei.aromara.brazier.aromara.confusion: Hostile creatures turn on each other; players nearby may gain warp.
jei.aromara.brazier.aromara.purge_taint: Drains flux and sets tainted creatures alight; in rain it can spill flux goo.
jei.aromara.info.candle_vat: Made by using a Heating Element on a crucible. Needs Ignis essentia piped into its bottom face. Melt a flesh block, add salis mundus, then a dried bundle; scoop the scented oil with an empty Scent Phial before it turns rancid.
jei.aromara.info.heating_element: Use it on a Thaumaturge crucible to turn the crucible into a Candle Vat.
jei.aromara.info.research_brief: Handed out by Aromara's hypothesis research. Place it on a Servoscrivener to read the riddle.
jei.aromara.info.servoscrivener: Not crafted: throw its ritual offerings into a lesser Crimson portal once you know the research, then destroy the portal. It sets riddles on research briefs.
jei.aromara.info.vishroom_cap: Grows as huge vishrooms in magical forests.
jei.aromara.info.vishroom_stem: Grows as huge vishrooms in magical forests.
jei.aromara.pressing.note: Wand it to press; one quartz nugget per crystal
message.aromara.brazier.no_ignis: Not enough ignis in your wand to light the brazier
message.aromara.scrivener.unknown: The Servoscrivener cannot make sense of this brief
research.aromara.aromatic_oils.stage_0: The vapours are fleeting and the brazier cannot follow me into battle. I need to trap a scent in something I can carry, even wear. Fat holds a smell for a long time. The walking dead are an endless source of it, and the blaze knows how to melt anything.
research.aromara.aromatic_oils.stage_1: Rendered flesh boiled with a dried bundle should take on its scent and keep it. Another brief for the Servoscrivener; its answer opens Imbuing Scents.
research.aromara.aromatic_oils.title: Hypothesis: Aromatic Oils
research.aromara.aromatic_vapors.stage_0: If scent can fight flux, the three magical plants that grow where the aura runs strong should do it far better than any mundane flower. I need living samples of each, and a careful look at them through the thaumometer.
research.aromara.aromatic_vapors.stage_1:
Each plant carries its aspects close to the surface. Dried and burned, they ought to release them into the air as a vapour, and every vapour should behave differently.
I have written the question up as a Research Brief. The Servoscrivener will turn it into a riddle; the finished brief opens Burning Scents.
research.aromara.aromatic_vapors.title: Hypothesis: Aromatic Vapours
research.aromara.miasma_theory.stage_0: I have learned to ignore what comes off the crucible, for most of what I melt smells sweet enough. Flux is different. Its stench is like nothing in the mundane world, and it sets my muscles twitching.
research.aromara.miasma_theory.stage_1: The first time I breathed it I pressed an ink-stained page to my face, and the headache faded. The old physicians blamed disease on bad air. Perhaps they were half right: if foul vapours carry flux, taint and warp, good ones might carry them away. These pages will hold what I find about magical aromas.
research.aromara.miasma_theory.title: Miasma Theory
research.aromara.scent_boiling.stage_0: Rotten flesh renders faster and gives more fat than any honest meat, which is fortunate, because I have no wish to waste good pork. The process needs steady heat that I can feed into a crucible from outside.
research.aromara.scent_boiling.stage_1: A Heating Element used on a crucible turns it into a Candle Vat. It no longer heats for free: it burns ignis essentia, drawn up a tube into its underside.
research.aromara.scent_boiling.stage_2:
Drop a block of flesh into the heated vat and let it melt; that takes two minutes. The moment it melts the fat starts to turn rancid, so within ten seconds add salis mundus to take the stink out. Then drop in a dried bundle. Two minutes later the fat turns a pleasant pink. Scoop it with a Scent Phial within ten seconds, before it spoils.
A filled phial and one piece of gear in a crafting grid oil the gear.

Cinderpearl suits armour: when I catch fire, every hostile creature within ten blocks burns too, two seconds for each oiled piece I wear.

Shimmerleaf suits tools: an oiled tool that would break keeps its last point of durability and takes a little of my hunger instead.

Vishroom suits armour: its fumes muddle anyone who swings at me. Each oiled piece is a one-in-twenty chance that the blow misses.

Rancid oil does nothing but announce itself.
research.aromara.scent_boiling.title: Imbuing Scents
research.aromara.scent_burning.stage_0: A plant must be dry before it burns sweetly, and drying it slowly wastes what it holds. A nitor sealed away from the air pulls aspects out of things; with a vis resonator to guide it, it might pull them out as crystals instead of letting them rot into flux. The Servoscrivener's answer to my brief should tell me how.
research.aromara.scent_burning.stage_1:
Four sprigs of one plant tied with string make a Redolent Bundle.
The Pressing Stone dries it. Put quartz nuggets into the stone and a fresh bundle under it, then strike it with your wand. It presses for three minutes, and now and then pushes one of the plant's aspects out of the top as an essentia crystal, using up a nugget. Some of what it squeezes out escapes as flux.
The Arcane Brazier burns coal, and nothing else, twice as fast as a furnace. Give it coal and a dried bundle, then light it with your wand; that costs a little ignis. Every coal it burns spreads the vapour ten blocks around.

Cinderpearl: the vapour burns flux out of the air, eases the pressure of creeping taint, and sets tainted creatures alight. In the rain, though, the flux it gathers falls as goo.

Shimmerleaf: those near the brazier stop feeling hungry, and the aura pays for every mouthful in vis.

Vishroom: hostile creatures lose track of friend and foe and fall on each other. Mind the creepers. Breathing it yourself may leave you seeing things.
research.aromara.scent_burning.title: Burning Scents
research.aromara.servoscrivener.stage_0:
What is this? I don't remember this page being here.
Ever since I first met the Crimson Cult I have wondered what lies on the other side of their portals. Their rites hold no answer for me, so I will try another way: feed the little portal something of a thinking man. A brain to think with, scribing tools to write with, and an ender pearl to find the way back. If each of them is thrown in by my own hand, the portal might bring something out of the void when it collapses.
research.aromara.servoscrivener.stage_1: I can't say what the brain saw in that violet abyss, but it taught me nothing. Instead I now own a strange device: a research table with a small mechanised arm that holds a quill. I should take a proper look at it with the thaumometer.
research.aromara.servoscrivener.stage_2:
I have worked out what the Servoscrivener, as I call it, can do. It can carry out my Miasma Theory research for me. Or, well, almost.
Each entry marked as a hypothesis gives me a Research Brief. Put it on the Servoscrivener and after a moment it sets me a riddle. The coloured words each stand for an aspect, and the number beside each word is how much of it the machine wants. I have to work out which aspect each word means.
Then I fill a jar with that essentia within ten blocks of the Servoscrivener and empty it (crouch and use the jar with an empty hand). If I guessed right the vapour goes into the riddle and does not turn into flux. When every word is paid for, the finished brief pops out of the top.
Use the machine with an empty hand to hear the riddle again, or crouch to take the brief back.

Addendum
A mind corrupted by the void is not a careful one. Ordinary paper would be torn to shreds by its scribbling, so I made a tougher Parchment for my briefs.
